questions.q: In this lab's scenario, why does the company need a custom action instead of an official spoke?
options: The inventory system already has an official spoke, but it's misconfigured
The niche internal inventory system has no official ServiceNow spoke
The company's instance doesn't support generic REST steps
Custom actions are required for every integration, regardless of whether a spoke exists
questions.explain: A custom action is the right tool specifically because no official spoke covers this homegrown inventory system.

questions.q: What single Input does "Check Inventory Level" require, and why only that one?
options: A full set of warehouse location, API key, and SKU, so the consumer handles everything
No Inputs at all — the action checks every item automatically
Item SKU — because that's the only thing a flow builder actually needs to supply to ask the question
The Authentication Profile's credentials, entered directly by the flow builder
questions.explain: The action deliberately keeps the Input surface minimal — warehouse details and credentials belong to the internal step and Authentication Profile, not the consumer.

questions.q: How does the internal REST step authenticate against the inventory system?
options: By referencing an Authentication Profile already configured in Chapter 3, rather than re-entering credentials
By asking the flow builder to type a password each time the action runs
It doesn't authenticate at all, since it's an internal system
By using the MID Server exclusively, with no Authentication Profile
questions.explain: The action reuses a Chapter 3 Authentication Profile internally, so every consuming flow inherits correct authentication automatically.

questions.q: The inventory API returns sku, qty_available, and warehouse. Which does the action expose as an Output, and why?
options: None of them — Outputs are optional and this action has none
Only Quantity Available, because that's the only field a consuming flow actually needs to act on
All three fields, because more data is always better for the consumer
Only warehouse, since location matters most
questions.explain: The action maps and exposes only Quantity Available; sku and warehouse stay internal implementation details.

questions.q: Per the lab's sanity-check step, what should the Authentication Profile used inside the action be?
options: A personal credential belonging to whoever built the action
Hard-coded directly into the Output mapping
A shared service account meant for ongoing use, not a personal token tied to one person
Left blank, since the action doesn't need to authenticate
questions.explain: A personal token can break or get revoked when someone leaves; a shared, durable Authentication Profile is the safe choice for a published, reused action.
